Show the variable list of a dataset

Source: R/variables.R
variables.Rd

  • variables() works like the "Variables" tab in Stata.

  • variables_search() searches for variables by name or variable label, rather than by the values stored in the columns.

Usage

variables(.data, ...)

variables_search(.data, string, ...)

Arguments

.data

The input data frame, tibble, or data.table.

...

<tidy-select> Existing columns to select or rename before listing or searching. Omit to include all columns. Computed columns are not created by this argument.

string

A single non-missing character string to search for in names or labels. Search is case-insensitive and matches substrings by default. An empty string matches all selected variables. Wildcards *, ?, and ~ represent zero or more, exactly one, and one or more characters, respectively. Use ^ and $ anchors to require a complete name or label match.

Value

A table with a character name column. A character label column is added only when at least one selected variable has a usable label; unlabelled variables then have NA labels. Search returns only matching rows, in selection order, with the same columns as the selected variable list. Tables preserve the input's data.frame, tibble, or data.table container and supported preview settings. Results are ungrouped; arbitrary subclasses are not reconstructed on the inventory rows.

Details

Variable labels are read from each column's label attribute, including ordinary vectors without a labelled class. A usable label is a single, non-missing value that converts to nonempty text. Value-label mappings and cell values are not searched. Selecting or renaming columns retains their variable labels; the input data are not modified.

Selection follows dplyr::select(). On grouped data frames, grouping columns are retained and may produce a message when not explicitly selected. Ungroup first to search only independently selected columns.

Search patterns are translated before matching. One bracketed letter range such as [a-h], or ascending nonnegative integer range such as [1-12], is supported. Multiple bracketed ranges are unsupported. Numeric ranges are expanded into alternatives, so use unanchored patterns such as item[1-12] for substring matching. This pattern language is not a general-purpose regular-expression interface; invalid patterns produce an error.

See also

ds(), codebook(), browse()

Other inspection functions: browse(), codebook(), misstable(), names, var_type()

Examples

variables(lifeexp)
#> # A tibble: 6 × 2
#>   name      label                   
#>   <chr>     <chr>                   
#> 1 region    Region                  
#> 2 country   Country                 
#> 3 popgrowth Avg. annual % growth    
#> 4 lexp      Life expectancy at birth
#> 5 gnppc     GNP per capita          
#> 6 safewater Safe water              
variables_search(lifeexp, "n")
#> # A tibble: 5 × 2
#>   name      label                   
#>   <chr>     <chr>                   
#> 1 region    Region                  
#> 2 country   Country                 
#> 3 popgrowth Avg. annual % growth    
#> 4 lexp      Life expectancy at birth
#> 5 gnppc     GNP per capita          
variables_search(lifeexp, "^country$")
#> # A tibble: 1 × 2
#>   name    label  
#>   <chr>   <chr>  
#> 1 country Country

# Inspect metadata before choosing columns for subsequent analysis.
survey <- tibble::tibble(age = c(30, 45), income = c(2000, 3000))
attr(survey$income, "label") <- "Monthly earnings"
variables(survey, earnings = income, age)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 2
#>   name     label           
#>   <chr>    <chr>           
#> 1 earnings Monthly earnings
#> 2 age      NA              
variables_search(survey, "earn")
#> # A tibble: 1 × 2
#>   name   label           
#>   <chr>  <chr>           
#> 1 income Monthly earnings
